subject: general
question: Which Indian River that starts from Gangotri is polluted largely by human activities and industries?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Ganga__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gangotri glacier** is one of the **primary sources** of the river **Ganga.**
 
• Over the years, Ganga has been** largely polluted** by human activities and industries. 
 
• Ganga river is **severely polluting,** in regard to which Ganga Action Plan was launched.
 
• **Industrial waste **is the main cause of pollution in the Ganga.
 
• Numerous businesses that produce things like **rubber, plastic, and leather** have popped up along the river's bank and dump their trash into the water.
 
• **Life beneath the ocean **suffers as a result.
 
• **Fish growth** has substantially slowed.
 
• A recent survey estimates that the river receives almost **1 billion gallons of raw, untreated sewage.**

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **​Cauvery:**

 
 
• ​Cauveri or** Kaveri River** is a significant river in India that runs through the states of **Tamil Nadu and Karnataka**.
 
• **Talakaveri,** in the Brahmagiri range of the** Western Ghats**, Kodagu district in the state of Karnataka, is where the Kaveri River rises.
 
• The elevation of the Cauvery River is **1,341 metres.**
 
• The river's whole** length**, from its source to its outfall, is **800 km**.
 
 
 
• **Krishna:** 
 
 
• The **Krishna River,** which flows through the **Deccan Plateau**, is India's third-longest river after the Ganges and the Godavari.
 
• After the Ganges, Indus, and Godavari, it is also the **fourth-largest river basin** in terms of water inflows. 
 
• The 1,400 km (870 mi) long river is commonly known as **Krishnaveni**.
 
• It is **one of the largest rivers** in central-southern India.
 
 
 
• **Brahmapurta:**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra is a **trans-boundary river **that passes through Tibet, Bangladesh, and Northeastern India. 
 
• The Brahmaputra River **rises in the vast glacier mass** south of Konggyu Tsho Lake and north of the Kailash mountains of the Himalayas (5,150 m).
 
• Additionally it is known as the **Yarlung Tsangpo** in Tibetan, **Siang/Dihang River** in Arunachali, **Luit and Brahmaputra** in Assamese, and Jamuna River in Bangla.
 
• By discharge, it is the **ninth-largest river** in the world.
